topic: Pure Fourier Series: Decoding the Language of Waves

outline.topic: Pure Fourier Series: Decoding the Language of Waves

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Symphony of Waves
sections.content: Introduce the core concept: any complex periodic signal can be decomposed into a sum of simple sine and cosine waves. Use the analogy of a chord in music where a single sound is actually composed of multiple distinct frequencies.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Square Wave' being constructed by adding layers of sine waves (Fundamental + 3rd Harmonic + 5th Harmonic...).

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Orthogonality of Sine/Cosine
sections.content: Briefly define orthogonality as the mathematical 'independence' of functions. Explain that just as X and Y axes are independent, sine and cosine functions at different frequencies have zero correlation over a period, allowing us to 'extract' specific components.
sections.example: An animation showing two sine waves of different frequencies multiplying to cover a net area of zero over a full period.

sections.title: The Mathematical Framework: Fourier Coefficients
sections.content: Present the Fourier Series formula. Focus on the physical meaning of the coefficients (a_n, b_n): they act as 'volume knobs' that tell you how much of each specific frequency is present in the original signal.
sections.example: A GUI interface showing a signal on the left and a bar chart (frequency spectrum) on the right that grows as we calculate each coefficient.

sections.title: Application: Animal Vocalization Analysis
sections.content: Apply the theory to a real-world scenario. Explain how a bat’s chirps or a bird's song can be translated into a 'frequency signature' using Fourier analysis to identify species or communication patterns.
sections.example: A visual spectrogram showing a bat's complex click signal being decomposed into a clean bar chart representing the frequency components that allow the bat to 'see' in the dark.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Recap: Fourier series is the bridge between the Time Domain (how a wave changes over time) and the Frequency Domain (what ingredients make up the wave).
sections.example: A side-by-side animation: Left side shows a noisy wave oscillating; right side shows a stable, static bar chart identifying the 'pure' notes hidden inside the noise.

storyboard.title: Intuitive Hook: The Symphony of Waves
lecture_lines: Complex signals are sums of simple sine waves.
Think of a chord made of many frequencies.
A square wave is built from harmonic layers.
animations: Create visual of a single sine wave moving across screen. Color: #00FF00 (green).
Superimpose multiple sine waves with different frequencies. Color: #00FFFF (cyan).
Combine waves to show complex signal formation. Color: #FFFFFF (white).

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Review: The Orthogonality of Sine/Cosine
lecture_lines: Orthogonality means mathematical independence of functions.
Sine and cosine waves are mutually independent.
This independence allows us to extract signal components.
animations: Show two sine waves with distinct frequencies. Color: #FF00FF (magenta).
Demonstrate their product integral is zero. Color: #FFFF00 (yellow).
Highlight overlapping area fading to zero. Color: #FF0000 (red).

storyboard.title: The Mathematical Framework: Fourier Coefficients
lecture_lines: Fourier coefficients act as frequency volume knobs.
They quantify the presence of specific frequencies.
The spectrum grows as we calculate coefficients.
animations: Display Fourier Series formula clearly. Color: #FFFFFF (white).
Visualize each coefficient as a weight. Color: #00FF00 (green).
Animate weights scaling individual component waves. Color: #00FFFF (cyan).
Synthesize these into a single signal. Color: #FFA500 (orange).
Final signal matches original input pattern. Color: #FFFFFF (white).

storyboard.title: Application: Animal Vocalization Analysis
lecture_lines: Fourier analysis identifies animal vocalization signatures.
Bat chirps translate into unique frequency charts.
Spectrograms reveal patterns used for communication.
animations: Show raw bird chirp waveform on screen. Color: #00FF00 (green).
Compute FFT to show frequency bars. Color: #00FFFF (cyan).
Highlight dominant frequency peak in spectrum. Color: #FF0000 (red).

storyboard.title: Summary & Synthesis
lecture_lines: Fourier series bridges time and frequency domains.
Time domain shows waves changing over time.
Frequency domain reveals the signal's core ingredients.
animations: Recap key concepts: Orthogonality and Decomposition. Color: #FFFFFF (white).
Show signal transitioning back to components. Color: #00FFFF (cyan).
Final display of Fourier series power. Color: #FF0000 (red).
